sections.title: Hook/Introduction
sections.narration_text: Ever wondered how to find the longest side of a triangle?
sections.visual_description: Show a triangle with a question mark on the hypotenuse

sections.title: Foundation
sections.narration_text: It all starts with right-angled triangles, where one angle is 90 degrees.
sections.visual_description: Animate a right-angled triangle forming, highlighting the 90-degree angle

sections.title: Core Concept 1
sections.narration_text: The Pythagorean Theorem states that a squared plus b squared equals c squared.
sections.visual_description: Show the equation a^2 + b^2 = c^2 appearing on screen, with 'a' and 'b' labeled on the triangle's legs and 'c' on the hypotenuse

sections.title: Core Concept 2
sections.narration_text: This relationship holds true for all right-angled triangles, no matter the size.
sections.visual_description: Animate different sized right-angled triangles, with the equation still holding true for each

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.narration_text: The theorem helps us find the longest side, making it a fundamental tool in geometry.
sections.visual_description: Highlight the hypotenuse, with the equation solving for 'c' on screen

sections.title: Example/Application
sections.narration_text: For example, if a is 3 and b is 4, we can calculate c using the theorem.
sections.visual_description: Show a triangle with 'a' as 3 and 'b' as 4, then calculate 'c' on screen using the equation, resulting in c = 5

sections.title: Summary
sections.narration_text: The Pythagorean Theorem: a powerful tool for finding the longest side of any right-angled triangle.
sections.visual_description: Show the equation one last time, with a triangle and the solved example still on screen
